newsitem.title: USA: SEC eyes possible yield burning in 25 PA offerings.
newsitem.headline: SEC eyes possible yield burning in 25 PA offerings.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission subpoenad Allentown, Whitehall Township, and as many as 23 other Pennsylvania authorities to determine if "yield burning" occurred in 1990s refunding deals, city officials said.

Jack Meyers, assistant executive for Whitehall Township, told Reuters that SEC's Philadelphia office requested documents in February for a $4.94 million bond refunding handled in 1993 by Meridian Capital Markets, which was purchased last year by CoreStates Financial Corp.
CoreStates Financial Corp officials were unavailable for comment.

Linda Bodner, Allentown's director of finance, said SEC requested documents "several weeks ago" concerning a $31.5 million refunding in 1995, which also was handled by then Meridian, whose new company is based in Reading, Pa.

The $1.3 trillion municipal bond market has been rocked by allegations that bond underwriters overcharge issuers for U.S. Treasuries bought in the open market and used in bond financing transactions, a practice dubbed "yield burning."

The Internal Revenue Service last July told states and localities that they can avoid enforcement action if they rebate yield burning profits they made on the deals. Issuers said the plan is unfair because underwriters, in most cases, kept the markups secret.
Meyers said he was told by a CoreStates representative that the SEC is examining documents for a total of 25 deals handled by Meridian in Pennsylvania.
